extraction.name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
extraction.description: A large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization using SMPL body models. The dataset contains over 40 hours of motion data, spanning over 300 subjects, more than 11000 motions.
extraction.creator: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black
extraction.publisher: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems
extraction.citeAs: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, and Michael J. Black. AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes. In International Conference on Computer Vision, pages 5442-5451, 2019.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset unifies 15 existing optical marker-based motion capture datasets by converting them to a common SMPL representation using the MoSh++ method. Data was collected from multiple sources including publicly available datasets downloaded from the internet, privately obtained datasets, and datasets recorded by the authors themselves.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: During a mocap session, markers may get occluded by the body due to pose. If multiple markers of a particular body part are occluded simultaneously, the optimization may result in unreliable and implausible poses. A weight-balancing factor q is introduced to adjust the pose prior weight as a factor of the number of missing markers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of optical marker-based motion capture data from 15 different datasets. Each dataset was recorded using different numbers of markers (ranging from 37 to 91 markers) placed at different locations on the body.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: MoSh++ converts mocap marker data into SMPL body model parameters through a two-stage optimization process. Stage I optimizes poses, shape, and latent marker positions for randomly chosen frames. Stage II optimizes pose and soft-tissue deformation coefficients for each frame while keeping shape constant.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Due to inherent problems with mocap, such as swapped and mislabeled markers, results were manually inspected and either corrected or held out. The data was converted from varying marker sets to a unified SMPL representation including pose (159 parameters), shape (16 dimensions), and soft-tissue deformation (8 dimensions) parameters.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: MoSh++ method using SMPL-H body model, DMPL for soft-tissue deformations, MANO hand model, Chumpy autodifferentiation package, Powell's gradient based dogleg minimization
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be continuously expanded with more mocap data contributed by the authors and the community. The dataset is publicly available to the research community and the authors will support the community in adding new captures as long as they can be similarly shared.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains body shape information captured from 346 subjects. Two of the three subjects in the SSM dataset were professional models who signed modeling contracts allowing release of their 4D scan data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to marker-based motion capture data. Current runtime for MoSh++ is not real-time. The method has inherent problems with mocap such as swapped and mislabeled markers which required manual inspection and correction.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset can be used for animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning. It is useful for tasks including generating synthetic training for computer vision tasks. Users can adapt the data to different problems, produce high-quality animations, and train computer vision algorithms.
